description: The only surviving Ki-84 in the world; recovered by US forces in the Philippines in 1945 restored to flying condition by Planes of Fame and given to Japan in 1973; held successively by Fuji Heavy Industries at Utsunomiya the Arashiyama Museum in Kyoto and Shirahama in Wakayama before Chiran Town bought it; now owned by Minamikyushu City; certified 重要航空遺産 on 2023-02-14; photography is forbidden; the long-standing story that its wing spar was cut is refuted by the museum's own 2022 conservation survey which found no evidence of any cut outside the designed break points
aliases: Ki84; Ki-84-Ia; Hayate; Frank; 四式戦闘機一型甲; c/n 1446; Ki84Ia
museum_name: Chiran Peace Museum for Kamikaze Pilots

description: Forward half of the airframe only; ditched in May 1945 after engine failure and raised from off Tenouchi harbour Shimo-Koshikijima on 1980-06-12; the rear fuselage tore off on ditching and was lost; deliberately NOT restored and shown in as-recovered condition; the only exhibit inside the hall that may be photographed
aliases: A6M5c; 零式艦上戦闘機52型丙; Zeke
museum_name: Chiran Peace Museum for Kamikaze Pilots

description: Outdoor and photographable at any time; JASDF free-loan airframe; withdrawn at Hofu-Kita in 2005 and installed in May 2005 replacing T-6G 52-0120; originally in standard colours and later painted overall silver retaining only the roundels the serial and the fin unit badge
